Cross-cutting primary evidence

Accessed 2026-11-04. Research is targeted to decisions affecting the academic frontend. It is not a national LMS survey, a competitor execution benchmark or a legal/accessibility audit. Findings are short paraphrases; the full public pages remain with their publishers. Requirements elsewhere are Whiteboard design proposals, not verbatim vendor specifications.

Method and interpretation

The review began with the project's accepted academic concepts and the coworker gap assessment, then examined public primary documentation for grading, groups, calendars, submission and accessibility. Shared/student and staff evidence tables record the domain sources. Duplicate URLs across tables are one source, not independent corroboration. Publication dates are recorded only when explicitly shown; search crawl dates are not publication dates.

The result is a proposed page/task/state inventory. Its priorities are product judgments. No real student work, class data, private PDF or school credentials were sent to search tools. No paid research APIs or private competitor accounts were used. The coworker's reported Blackboard frustration is retained as a workflow observation, while current official documentation establishes that weighting and groups are supported capabilities.

Local sources

The original design tokens/components, academic batch renderers, canonical S/P map, D1-D65 decisions, source contract and normalized coworker review informed the proposal. resources/README.md identifies exact included files and their SHA-256 provenance. Original sources are references, not a new production architecture. More complete proposed W specifications supersede their academic gaps for this handoff; they do not retroactively mark old designs/browser checks as implemented or passed.
